column3: Close to the Hebrew; “it was broken into, the city” is rendered “the city was penetrated.”
NKJV divides the names as “Samgar-Nebo, Sarsechim” and treats the titles Rab-saris (“chief official”) and Rab-mag as names, “Rabsaris” and “Rabmag.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the Arabah” is rendered “the plain.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he spoke with him judgments” is rendered “he pronounced judgment on him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “those who had fallen to him” is rendered “those who defected to him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “on that day” is rendered “at the same time.”
Close to the Hebrew; “set your eyes on him” is rendered “look after him.”
Close to the Hebrew; as in verse 3, the titles Rab-saris and Rab-mag are rendered as names, “Rabsaris” and “Rabmag.”
Close to the Hebrew; “to take him out to the house” is rendered “that he should take him home.”
Close to the Hebrew; “for harm” is rendered “for adversity,” and “they will happen before you” “they shall be performed … before you.”
Close to the Hebrew; “your life will be to you as plunder” is rendered “your life shall be as a prize to you.”
